## Requirements

<a id="Linked"></a>

### As many links as asked

`Linked` · `src/rules.ts:128` · status: **held**

Each node the rule judges has, one way, at least and at most the number of edges of this name given: an entry point that calls a third party is verified by a scenario. What it finds: each node with too few or too many, with the nodes it is linked to.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
({ counts }) => (sketch: GraphSketch, p: { nodes: Selector; edge: string; way?: Way; atLeast?: number; atMost?: number }): RuleFinding[] =>
    picked(sketch, p.nodes).flatMap((n) => {
      const out = (p.way ?? Direction.out) === Direction.out
      const others = sketch.edges
        .filter((e) => e.name === p.edge && (out ? e.from === n.ref : e.to === n.ref))
        .map((e) => (out ? e.to : e.from))
      const wrong = others.length < (p.atLeast ?? counts.zero) || (p.atMost !== undefined && others.length > p.atMost)
      return wrong ? [{ on: n.ref, nodes: others }] : []
    })
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Parameters: `counts` ← [Counts](algebra.md#Counts)
- Refines: [Rules applied, not written again](product.md#SharedRules)

<a id="NeverReaches"></a>

### A node never reaches what it must not

`NeverReaches` · `src/rules.ts:109` · status: **held**

No node the rule judges reaches, through edges of the names given, any node of the targets, even from afar: a renderer never reaches the graph. What it finds: each node that does, with the targets it reaches.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
({ counts }) => (sketch: GraphSketch, p: { nodes: Selector; through: readonly string[]; to: Selector; way?: Way }): RuleFinding[] => {
    const targets = new Set(picked(sketch, { libraries: true, ...p.to }).map((n) => n.ref))
    return picked(sketch, p.nodes).flatMap((n) => {
      const hit = [...reached(sketch, n.ref, p.through, p.way ?? Direction.out)].filter((r) => targets.has(r))
      return counts.any(hit) ? [{ on: n.ref, nodes: hit }] : []
    })
  }
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Parameters: `counts` ← [Counts](algebra.md#Counts)
- Refines: [Rules applied, not written again](product.md#SharedRules)

<a id="Reaches"></a>

### A node reaches what it must

`Reaches` · `src/rules.ts:93` · status: **held**

Each node the rule judges reaches, through edges of the names given (followed one way, from node to node), at least one node of the targets: an ADR serves a goal, code reaches a requirement or an ADR. What it finds: each node that reaches none.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
() => (sketch: GraphSketch, p: { nodes: Selector; through: readonly string[]; to: Selector; way?: Way }): RuleFinding[] => {
    const targets = new Set(picked(sketch, { libraries: true, ...p.to }).map((n) => n.ref))
    return picked(sketch, p.nodes)
      .filter((n) => ![...reached(sketch, n.ref, p.through, p.way ?? Direction.out)].some((r) => targets.has(r)))
      .map((n) => ({ on: n.ref }))
  }
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Refines: [Rules applied, not written again](product.md#SharedRules)

<a id="WithoutEffects"></a>

### Effects a node may not have

`WithoutEffects` · `src/rules.ts:149` · status: **held**

No node the rule judges has one of these effects, its own or through what it depends on: a read writes nothing, an engine function does not write to disk. What it finds: each node that has some, with the effects and the dependencies that bring them.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
({ counts }) => (sketch: GraphSketch, p: { nodes: Selector; effects: readonly string[]; dependency?: string }): RuleFinding[] =>
    picked(sketch, p.nodes).flatMap((n) => {
      const bad = p.effects.filter((e) => n.effects.includes(e))
      if (counts.isEmpty(bad)) return []
      const byRef = new Map(sketch.nodes.map((x) => [x.ref, x]))
      const carriers = sketch.edges
        .filter((e) => e.from === n.ref && e.name === (p.dependency ?? EdgeName.deps))
        .map((e) => byRef.get(e.to))
        .filter((d): d is SketchNode => d !== undefined && d.effects.some((x) => bad.includes(x)))
        .map((d) => d.ref)
      return [{ on: n.ref, words: bad, nodes: carriers }]
    })
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Parameters: `counts` ← [Counts](algebra.md#Counts)
- Refines: [Rules applied, not written again](product.md#SharedRules)

<a id="WordsOf"></a>

### Words of a vocabulary

`WordsOf` · `src/rules.ts:172` · status: **held**

The words a node lists in a field (the effects a port declares) are words of a vocabulary, or of the words given besides. What it finds: each node with words that are not, and those words.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
({ counts }) => (sketch: GraphSketch, p: { nodes: Selector; field: string; vocabulary: SketchNode; also?: readonly string[] }): RuleFinding[] => {
    const known = new Set([...Object.keys((p.vocabulary.field(VocabularyField.words) as Record<string, unknown> | undefined) ?? {}), ...(p.also ?? [])])
    // A field holds a list of words, or lists by name (the effects of a port, method by method).
    const listed = (v: unknown): readonly string[] =>
      Array.isArray(v) ? v : v instanceof Object ? Object.values(v).flatMap((x) => (Array.isArray(x) ? x : [])) : []
    return picked(sketch, p.nodes).flatMap((n) => {
      const words = listed(n.field(p.field)).filter((w) => !known.has(w))
      return counts.any(words) ? [{ on: n.ref, words }] : []
    })
  }
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Parameters: `counts` ← [Counts](algebra.md#Counts)
- Refines: [Rules applied, not written again](product.md#SharedRules)

## Vocabulary

<a id="Directions"></a>

### Directions

`Directions` · `src/rules.ts:22`

Which way a rule follows an edge: from the node it judges to the node the edge leads to, or from a node whose edge leads to it. A rule's parameters name a direction by one of these words (`way: "in"`), checked by the compiler.

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `out` | From the node, along the edge: what it serves, what it depends on |
| `in` | Toward the node, against the edge: what serves it, what depends on it |
